items.title: What pyhabitats is
items.text: It is a Python library designed for habitat analysis of radiomic images. It provides an interface for such analysis pipeline from loading images from disk, through identifying habitats to radiomic features extraction. It offers predefined clusterization algorithms for habitat identification and support custom ones.

items.title: Main features
items.text:
Library provides the following features:

  1. Loading medical images from disk. Supports wide range of formats designed for medical imaging (e.g. .nii.gz, .nrrd, .png and more).
  2. Habitats identification. Uses clusterization algorithms to find similar sub-regions in ROI (region of interest). The number of habitats can be provided by user.
  3. Radiomic features extraction. Utilizes pyradiomics library to extract radiomic features for each identified habitat.

items.title: pyhabitats.cluster_algorithm
items.text:
Defines type definitions for clustering algorithms.

This module provides the necessary typing interfaces to support both standard scikit-learn clustering algorithms and custom implementations within the habitat analysis pipeline.

@runtime_checkable
class CustomClusterAlgorithm(Protocol):
    """Protocol for custom clustering algorithms.

    Defines the required interface for custom clustering algorithms,
    ensuring they provide a fitting mechanism and expose the resulting cluster labels
    in a manner compatible with standard implementations.

    Attributes:
        labels (np.ndarray | None): An array of cluster labels assigned to the input
            data after the model is fitted. Typically remains `None` until `fit` is
            called.
    """

    labels: np.ndarray | None = None

    def fit(self, X: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Fits the clustering algorithm to the provided training data.

        Args:
            X (Any): The training input samples (e.g., an array of features).
            **kwargs (Any): Additional keyword arguments for the fitting process.

        Returns:
            Any: The fitted instance of the algorithm (typically `self`).
        """

class FeaturesExtractor:
    """Radiomic features extractor.

    Utilizes a pyradiomics extractor to compute features for
    different habitats defined by the input mask, aggregating
    the results into a single dataset.

    Args:
        params (dict | None, optional): Configuration parameters for the analysis
            pipeline. Specifies filters applied to image and features to extract.
            Configuration is compatible with pyradiomics configuration
            (see: https://pyradiomics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/customization.html).
            Defaults to `None`.
    """

    def __init__(self, params: dict | None = None) -> None:
        self.params = params

    def execute(self, image: np.ndarray, mask: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Executes the feature extraction process on the given image and mask.

        Initializes the pyradiomics extractor, runs the extraction
        process for each distinct habitat defined in the mask, and concatenates
        the computed features into a single DataFrame.

        Args:
            image (np.ndarray): An input image array.
            mask (np.ndarray): An input mask array defining the habitat regions.
                Must contain integer values where 0 represents background and positive
                values represent habitats.

        Returns:
            pd.DataFrame: A DataFrame containing the results of the habitat analysis.
                Each row corresponds to one habitat identified by value in column
                `habitat_id`. Extracted radiomic features are stored in the remaining
                columns.
        """

items.title: HabitatAnalysisPipeline
items.text:
Pipeline for executing habitat analysis from loading raw images to features extraction.

Simplifies habitat analysis pipeline by wrapping ImageLoader, HabitatsExtractor and FeaturesExtractor into one object with simple, one-method API. Pipeline execution is equivalent to carrying out the subsequent steps of the analysis: 1. Loading raw image and mask from disk. 2. Applying clusterization algorithm to determine habitats. 3. Extracting radiomic features for each habitat.

Attributes:

Name Type Description habitats ndarray | None

Habitats mask determined during pipeline execution. Set to None before pipeline execution.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default params dict | None

Configuration parameters for the analysis pipeline. Specifies filters applied to image and radiomic features to extract. Configuration is compatible with pyradiomics configuration (see: https://pyradiomics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/customization.html). Defaults to None.

class HabitatAnalysisPipeline:
    """Pipeline for executing habitat analysis from loading raw images to features
    extraction.

    Simplifies habitat analysis pipeline by wrapping ImageLoader, HabitatsExtractor and
    FeaturesExtractor into one object with simple, one-method API. Pipeline execution is
    equivalent to carrying out the subsequent steps of the analysis:
    1. Loading raw image and mask from disk.
    2. Applying clusterization algorithm to determine habitats.
    3. Extracting radiomic features for each habitat.

    Attributes:
        habitats (np.ndarray | None): Habitats mask determined during pipeline execution.
            Set to `None` before pipeline execution.

    Args:
        params (dict | None, optional): Configuration parameters for the analysis
            pipeline. Specifies filters applied to image and radiomic features to
            extract. Configuration is compatible with pyradiomics configuration
            (see: https://pyradiomics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/customization.html).
            Defaults to `None`.
    """

    habitats: np.ndarray | None

    def __init__(self, params: dict | None = None) -> None:
        self.params = params
        self.habitats = None

    def execute(
        self,
        image_path: str,
        mask_path: str,
        habitats_number: int,
        algorithm: str | ClusterAlgorithm,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Executes the habitat analysis pipeline on the provided image and mask.

        Args:
            image_path (str): Path to the file or directory containing input image
                (images).
            mask_path (str): Path to the input mask file. Mask must be binary and
                contain only zero and one values for, respectively, backgroud and
                region of interest.
            habitats_number (int): Number of habitats to identify. Must be positive.
                If set to one the computed habitat will be equal to mask input.
            algorithm (str | ClusterAlgorithm): The clustering algorithm to apply.

        Returns:
            pd.DataFrame: A DataFrame containing the results of the habitat analysis.
                Each row corresponds to one habitat identified by value in column
                `habitat_id`. Extracted radiomic features are stored in the remaining
                columns.
        """

items.title: HabitatsExtractor
items.text:
Extractor for identifying distinct habitats from image.

This class allows to specify number of habitats and clusterization algorithm used during extraction. Supports predefined algorithms and custom ones compatible with ClusterAlgorithm type.

Source code in src/pyhabitats/habitats_extractor.py 
class HabitatsExtractor:
    """Extractor for identifying distinct habitats from image.

    This class allows to specify number of habitats and clusterization algorithm
    used during extraction. Supports predefined algorithms and custom ones compatible
    with `ClusterAlgorithm` type.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._supported_algorithms = ["kmeans", "agglomerative"]
        self._loader = ImageLoader()

    def execute(
        self,
        image: np.ndarray,
        mask: np.ndarray,
        habitats_number: int,
        algorithm: str | ClusterAlgorithm,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Identifies habitats in image.

        Applies a specified clustering algorithm to the region of the input image
        defined by the provided mask. It partitions the masked pixels into the
        requested number of classes and generates a mask for each resulting cluster.

        Args:
            image (np.ndarray): A numpy array representing the image.
            mask (np.ndarray): A numpy array representing the mask. Must be
                binary.
            habitats_number (int): Number of habitats to extract. If set to 1, provided
                mask will be returned as output.
            algorithm (str | ClusterAlgorithm): Clusterization algorithm used for
                extraction.

        Returns:
            np.ndarray: A numpy array with extracted habitats. Each habitat is identified
                by positive, integer value 1, 2, 3 and so on. Background is identifed by value 0.
        """
        image_input = None
        mask_input = None
        if not isinstance(image_input, (str, np.ndarray)):
            raise TypeError(
                f"image_input must be a string representing a file path or a numpy array, got {type(image_input)}"
            )

        if not isinstance(mask_input, (str, np.ndarray)):
            raise TypeError(
                f"mask_input must be a string representing a file path or a numpy array, got {type(mask_input)}"
            )

        if not isinstance(habitats_number, int) or isinstance(habitats_number, bool):
            raise TypeError(
                f"habitats_number must be an integer, got {type(habitats_number)}"
            )

        if not isinstance(algorithm, (str, ClusterAlgorithm)):
            raise TypeError(
                f"algorithm must be a string from {self._supported_algorithms} or an instance of ClusterAlgorithm, got {type(algorithm)}"
            )

        image = self._get_image_from_input(image_input)
        mask = self._get_image_from_input(mask_input)
        alg = self._get_algorithm(algorithm, n_clusters=habitats_number)

        features_number = image.shape[-1] if image.ndim > 3 else 1
        alg.fit(image[mask == 1].reshape(-1, features_number))

        habitats = []

        labels = np.full_like(mask, -1, dtype=int)
        labels[mask == 1] = alg.labels_

        for i in range(habitats_number):
            habitat_mask = (labels == i) * 1
            habitat_mask = habitat_mask.astype(np.uint8)
            habitats.append(habitat_mask)

        return habitats

    def _get_image_from_input(self, input: str | np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        if isinstance(input, str):
            return self._loader.load_image(input)
        return input

    def _get_algorithm(
        self, algorithm: str | ClusterAlgorithm, **kwargs: dict[str, int]
    ) -> ClusterAlgorithm:
        """Returns the clustering algorithm based on the provided string.

        Args:
            algorithm: A string representing the desired clustering algorithm.

        Returns:
            An instance of the specified clustering algorithm.
        """
        if isinstance(algorithm, ClusterAlgorithm):
            return algorithm

        if algorithm == "kmeans":
            return KMeans(n_clusters=kwargs.get("n_clusters", 2))
        elif algorithm == "agglomerative":
            return AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=kwargs.get("n_clusters", 2))
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported algorithm: {algorithm}. Supported algorithms are: {self._supported_algorithms}"
            )

items.title: ImageLoader
items.text:
Medical images loader.

It can load files supported by SimpleITK (e.g. .nii, .nrrd, .jpg). Handles both single image files and directories containing multiple images. In the case of multiple images, loader stacks them into single numpy array.

Source code in src/pyhabitats/image_loader.py 
class ImageLoader:
    """Medical images loader.

    It can load files supported by SimpleITK (e.g. .nii, .nrrd, .jpg). Handles
    both single image files and directories containing multiple images. In the
    case of multiple images, loader stacks them into single numpy array.
    """

    def load_image(self, image_path: str) -> np.ndarray:
        """Loads image from a file or directory.

        Args:
            image_path (str): Path to the image file or a directory of images.

        Returns:
            np.ndarray: A numpy array representing the loaded image(s). Values
                inside the array represent features used in clusterization.
        """
        path = Path(image_path)

        if not path.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {image_path}")

        if path.is_file():
            return self._read_file(str(path))

        if path.is_dir():
            files = sorted([f for f in path.iterdir() if f.is_file()])

            if not files:
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"No files found in directory: {image_path}")

            arrays = [self._read_file(str(file)) for file in files]

            return np.stack(arrays, axis=-1)

    def _read_file(self, filepath: str) -> np.ndarray:
        image = sitk.ReadImage(filepath)
        array = sitk.GetArrayFromImage(image)
        return array
